newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Richemont trades 3 mln shares in asset swap.
newsitem.headline: Richemont trades 3 mln shares in asset swap.

text.p: South African tobacco stock, Richemont Securities, was active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Friday with more than three million shares trading in an asset swap deal, dealers said.
SMK Securities, the brokers that did the swap, said it had been carried out in three tranches. They declined to give further details.
JSE dealers said the first deal saw one million shares trade, followed by another in 1.7 million and a last batch of 350,000 stocks.
At 1110 GMT Richemont was unchanged at 64.50 rand having touched a high of 65 rand and a low of 63.75 and after more than 4.7 million shares had traded.
Traders said on Friday there had recently been a notable uptick in asset swap activity on the JSE.

"There have been more (swaps) than before...possibly with the rand having stuck in a tight band for the last month or three, foreigners are feeling buoyant about doing asset swaps with us," said Greg Amoils, a director of portfolio management at Irish & Menell Rosenberg.
"Our guys have always been willing to do it, but haven't always found willing partners on the other side," he added.
Old Mutual, South Africa's biggest investment group, said last week it was concluding a new asset swap programme to increase its offshore holdings.

The March budget gave institutions the go ahead to invest up to 10 percent of their total assets abroad, an increase on the previous limit of 10 percent of each individual mutual fund, known locally as unit trusts.
